1 big thing — Pope: Algorithms lack "spark of humanity"
 
Illustration: Brendan Lynch/Axios

Pope Leo XIV is calling for the Catholic Church to work with artists to protect human creativity amid a glut of AI-generated content, Axios' Herb Scribner reports.

🤳 Leo wrote on X: "In this era of artificial intelligence, it is becoming urgent to distinguish human art from what machines produce."

  • "There is an ontological difference, even before an aesthetic one, between art and what a machine can generate through statistical calculation based on millions of images created by others."
  • "Algorithms lack the spark of humanity."

🤖 Leo has spoken out about AI and its influence on humanity before.

  • In the first encyclical of his papacy, he said there was a need to "disarm" the technology to prevent it "from dominating humanity."
  • He approved the creation of an AI commission in May to coordinate the church's policies and work around the emerging technology.

Recently, Leo warned of a "paradise of machines" invading and taking over our daily activities. He also said that warnings from AI researchers should be "taken seriously."

  • He told reporters on Monday: "We have to keep working. We can't just sit back and pretend nothing is going to happen."

2. 💵 Exclusive: Bessent compares Trump Accounts to GI Bill
 
Photo: JaMar Jones for Axios

Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent told Mike Allen on "The Axios Show" that Trump Accounts will be the "most important benefit for young people since the GI Bill," Axios' Courtenay Brown reports.

🧒 Treasury this week automatically created Trump Accounts for more than 60 million children.

  • Bessent said in the interview at the Treasury Building that about 8 million people already created accounts before automatic enrollment.

💸 Bessent said the accounts could bring millions of new families into the financial markets.

  • He compared the lack of access to a "food desert," saying that families struggling to cover an unexpected expense are unlikely to open a brokerage account and start investing.
  • "By creating these accounts, we are opening this up."

🪖 Bessent's GI Bill comparison sets a high bar.

  • That program helped millions of World War II veterans pay for education and training and buy homes.

4. 🥅 1 sports thing: Goalie goal!
 
Igor Shesterkin attempts a shot against the Tampa Bay Lightning last night. Photo: Bruce Bennett/Getty Images

New York Rangers goaltender Igor Shesterkin last night became just the 18th netminder in NHL history to score a goal.

  • His third period volley into an open net put the Rangers up 5-1 against the Tampa Bay Lightning, sealing their home opener victory.

🏒 True "goalie goals" are so rare in hockey because they require a perfect setup — including an empty net after the opposing team pulls their goalie for an extra skater in a desperate bid for a late-game goal.
